text:
Amina (Support): Heads up — AcmePay reporting intermittent 401s on SSO callback around midnight UTC. They claim it started after their IdP maintenance window. Logs show both `invalid signature` and `kid not found` errors.
Jordan (Eng/Security): Can you paste the exact log lines and timestamps? Any pattern by region/timezone?
Amina (Support): Sure — snippets: 
```
2024-03-02T23:58:12Z ERROR auth verify_jwt: signature verification failed, kid=0x9f2, token=sub:acme-123
2024-03-02T23:58:13Z WARN jwks cache: candidate KID mismatch, cached_kids=[0x8a1], remote_kids=[0x9f2]
2024-03-02T23:58:14Z ERROR auth verify_jwt: jwt expired (exp=1709498280 now=1709499494)
```
Customer timezone is +11 (AUS). Fails spike ~23:58-00:05 UTC.
Ryan (Platform): Two likely interacting things: (1) IdP rotated keys during their maintenance and published a new JWKS, (2) some of our proxy instances kept a stale JWKS due to long cache TTL + no on-miss refresh. Also see one host with NTP drift ~+7m in our fleet recently.
sso-proxy-bot: JWKS fetch status: 200 OK, Cache-Control: max-age=86400, ETag: "v20240302-1"
Jordan (Eng/Security): That Cache-Control is huge — if the IdP rotated keys without changing the ETag or adding a cache-busting header, proxies will keep returning old keys until TTL expires. Combine that with a few hosts that have clock >5m drift and you get expired/invalid signature mixes.
Amina (Support): Repro steps requested by customer. What do we ask them to run?
Ryan (Platform): Ask them to: 1) curl the JWKS endpoint and verify kids list: `curl -sS https://idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'` 2) check token `kid` vs JWKS kids. 3) on their callback server run `date -u +%s` and compare to `curl -sI https://time.cloudflare.com` or an NTP check. 4) try forcing our proxy to refresh JWKS by hitting our admin endpoint: `POST /admin/proxy/refresh_jwks?issuer=idp.example` (we have this for emergency).
Jordan (Eng/Security): Also ask them to attach a raw failing token (strip sensitive sub/claims if needed) so we can re-run verification locally.
Amina (Support): Customer provided a token and jwks URL. I re-ran locally, saw `kid` present in remote JWKS but our locally cached file still used old key until I manually hit proxy refresh.
Jordan (Eng/Security): Root cause hypothesis: IdP rotated keys and kept long max-age; proxies follow Cache-Control strictly and didn't revalidate on 304 because ETag didn't change; a subset of our fleet had small clock skew causing some tokens to be treated as expired.
Ryan (Platform): Short-term mitigations: 1) trigger emergency proxy JWKS refresh for affected customers, 2) increase JWT verification leeway to 120s (config flag per-issuer), 3) rollout a proxy change to attempt `If-None-Match` revalidation on misses or fetch-on-miss.
Jordan (Eng/Security): Long-term: recommend adding robust on-miss JWKS refresh: when `kid` not found, immediately re-fetch JWKS from origin and retry verification once before failing. Also add telemetry to alert when `kid not found` spikes. For clock drift: ensure NTP enforcement and add host-level alert when monotonic skew >30s.
Amina (Support): For the customer: applied emergency refresh, asked them to verify. They still see a couple of 401s; I suspect some of their callback servers are in flight or cached upstream.
Ryan (Platform): If they're behind CDN, instruct to purge the JWKS cache there too or use a short cache-busting query param during rotation.
Jordan (Eng/Security): Quick code snippet we can share with customers to detect the issue: 
```
# check token kid vs jwks
TOKEN_KID=$(jq -R 'split(".") | .[0]' <<< "$TOKEN") || true
curl -sS https://idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json | jq -e ".keys[] | select(.kid==\"$TOKEN_KID\")" >/dev/null || echo "kid-mismatch"
```
Amina (Support): Customer confirms TTL on their CDN was 24h and IdP didn't change ETag during rotation. They're purging now.
Jordan (Eng/Security): Follow-up action items: - eng/platform: implement on-miss JWKS fetch + retry (priority P1) - infra: add NTP drift monitor (P2) - support: add a KB article with repro steps and mitigation (leeway, forced refresh, CDN purge).
Ryan (Platform): I'll open the PR for on-miss fetch, and add a circuit to avoid thundering-herd (linear backoff + singleflight).
Amina (Support): Filing ticket to AcmePay with steps we took and ETA for platform fix.
Jordan (Eng/Security): Nice catch. Save logs and correlate host IDs for skewed nodes so infra can remediate. :thumbsup:
Amina (Support): Closing loop with customer once spikes stop. :eyes:
